explanation.definitionFit: This flat pale legume is a pulse eaten as a vegetable, so it is a kind of food.

clue.text: Playwright increasingly poorly after a day in wing

clue.text: United played without fine international, preferring width

explanation.definitionFit: Metal pieces fused together by heat are joined, so welded means joined as one.

clue.text: Irvine Welsh's Ecstasy: Three Tales of Chemical Romance, that's read online?

explanation.walkthrough: The title of Welsh's book does double duty in the surface: its first word gives E and the volume itself is a BOOK.

clue.text: Styling for girl, with set locks the latest in fashion? Once

clue.text: Old canoeists turned blue

clue.text: Carnation, perhaps in Eton suit, thrown to floor

clue.text: Dashed around unknown town, offloading junk illicitly

clue.text: Born idle (not half), brought up in a different world?

definitions.text: Born idle (not half), brought up in a different world?

parts.note: nee means born, used before a maiden name

indicators.note: the reversed half of idle goes in the rearranged world letters
a different version of a word has its letters in another order
in a down clue brought up means read upwards, so backwards
not half means half of the word idle is dropped, here its first two letters

explanation.surface: Someone lazy from birth was raised in a completely different world.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue defines a born layabout. 'not half' halves idle, 'brought up' turns that half upwards, and 'different' scrambles world around it.
explanation.definitionFit: A layabout who never amounts to anything is an idle good-for-nothing.

clue.text: Soil outside of smalls after fly open regularly
